reports.title: Spooky turns      (Halloween spooky)
reports.comment:
quick: Good spooky turns high up (Halloween spooky). Parking to 2000m 5-10cm, 2000m to alp 15-50cm in immediate lees. Surprisingly good skiing up high. Minimal core shots on the ski out.
South slopes pretty bare. Just good enough.

reports.title: Healy Pass Conditions
reports.comment: quick: Early season tour up to Healy Pass today. Snow is remarkably good near the pass. 60cm HS. Good firm base at 40cm with 20cm light dry powder on top. Snowpack is well-consolidated. Snowed steadily all day, -4º. Thin near trailhead (5cm), but increases in depth with elevation. Trail is in great shape.

reports.title: Monarch Ramparts Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Surprisingly good early season skiing in the alpine. Conditions seem stable.

reports.title: 93 South
reports.comment:
quick: Great turns to be had on 93S! The snow depth is impressive for this time of year although not enough to make valley bottom bushwhacking anywhere near pleasant. / snowpack: Powder conditions with some soft wind slab forming at our top out point at 2100 m. No result on an isolated column test before dropping in. 

We observed one small dry loose in steep terrain.

reports.title: Verendrye Burn
reports.comment: quick: Skied fantastic powder in the burn by Verendrye, there’s plenty of tracks to be had if you’re looking in the right places.  We transitioned just at treeline, (~2050m) and skied both East and NW aspects. Noticed no evidence of wind transport, even on open slopes at treeline, however, there is a layer of surface hoar forming at all aspects and elevations we skied at. Hopefully some wind will …

reports.title: 93S- wind slab avalanche obsevation
reports.comment: quick: Slight suncrust on southeast facing slopes, nice powder below. Old tracks are rock hard / avalanche: Noted a size 1 just below ridge, appeared to be a day or two old. Suspected skier triggered as there were tracks above and below slide. Looked to be a wind slab.

reports.title: Size 1 Avalanche
reports.comment: avalanche: We were skiing a fairly wide ridge between two gullies and I went over a slight convexity and triggered a small slab avalanche. I was able to ski out of it to the side at the start zone. The debris covered some old tracks in the gully to the north.

reports.title: Floe Lake to Numa mountain
reports.comment: quick: Decent snow in sheltered higher elevations:  i got on all kinds of steep high alpine terrain today and couldn’t get anything moving besides the new 3cm of snow.

reports.title: Serac Col
reports.comment:

reports.title: Simpson
reports.comment: avalanche: Remote triggered an overhead convexity while traversing on a mellow bench.

reports.title: Wind slab
reports.comment: avalanche: Lots of whoomphing at TL and wind slabs starting to become reactive as the day went on. Just as forecasted.

reports.title: Surface hoar in Kootenay
reports.comment: quick: The Jan 24 surface hoar layer has become a significant avalanche problem in Kootenay as the slab over the weak layer has developed. Cracks are now easily propagating, avalanches to size 2 have been triggered this week, and avalanches have been observed in dense forest. And now a storm will add to this. Heads up; although the weak layer is one month old, the problem is coming to life now.

reports.title: Simpson burn
reports.comment: quick: We skied the Simpson burn, really good skiing to about 1600m. At 2100m HS is 230cm and there is 37cm of new snow, not bonding really well with the thick rain crust. The snow was becoming heavier in the afternoon, forming more of a slab. There was one natural size 1 out from a 40º roll, and we skied cut and triggered a few really predictable small size 1 sliding on the March 24 rain crust.

reports.title: North side of The Monarch
reports.comment: quick: Went to check out the multiple bowls and couloirs on the north side of The Monarch, but stuck to mellow tree skiing after being struck by a size 1  Na LD at the bottom of the northern most couloir. Overall good riding conditions with ~5 cm over previous crusts at TL. Most large features had released during the previous AR event, with many crowns and debris piles still visible. / avalanche: …
